newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION - PIENAAR MOVES TO U.K. WITH MANDELA BLESSING.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - PIENAAR MOVES TO U.K. WITH MANDELA BLESSING.

text.p: Deposed Springbok World Cup captain Francois Pienaar insisted on Tuesday he had not abandoned South African rugby despite becoming the latest big-name player to sign for ambitious London club Saracens.

Pienaar, 29, will team up with the world's leading pointscorer Michael Lynagh and Frenchman Philippe Sella, the most capped test player in history, following the latest bold initiative by Saracens' millionaire backer Nigel Wray.

The Transvaal flanker has been given a free transfer by the South African Rugby Football Union, a month after being dumped from the Springbok squad currently touring France, but has not given up all hope of a recall.

"I am determined to challenge for my place back in the South African national team and eventually go back home and put something back into South African rugby," said Pienaar, revealing he had spoken to President Nelson Mandela before signing the deal.
"I have phoned President Mandela and he is very sorry that I will be leaving South Africa. But I am going to represent South Africa in an ambassadorial role."

Pienaar, who will be 30 five days after launching the latest phase of his career on December 28, is expected to receive around 400,000 pounds from his two-year contract, which has an option of a third year.
"We took the decision only last night. I will be going back to South Africa to get things sorted out and we will be coming back for training just before Christmas.
"The English game has had many innovations this year but I hope I can bring something fresh as a representative of my country's rugby."
SARFU chief executive Rian Oberholzer confirmed in Johannesburg the move would not automatically spell the end of his test career.
"Francois Pienaar's presence on the playing fields of South Africa will be greatly missed, but the move does not exclude him from selection from the Springbok team in future," he said.
That means Pienaar could yet play against the British Lions in South Africa next year, although the Springboks are currently doing well without him in France.
"I would be thrilled about going back into the South African team against the Lions next year...or even for Transvaal," he said.

"When I was left out of the tour squad, I realised how much South Africa still meant to me even after the World Cup final. The support for me went on for weeks and I will never complain about criticism again.
"However, I am committed to Saracens and you have got to get over the hurt of being dropped. It was not nice and I would love to play for South Africa again.
"I am still hungry for rugby. I need rugby. Rugby does not need me."

Australian stand-off Lynagh welcomed the arrival of a respected former opponent. "He has hounded me on the test field and I am glad to know that he will be in the same coloured jersey. He is a fantastic player."
SARFU have confirmed that Pienaar's lucrative World Cup contract has been cancelled.
Details of the contract were never made public, but it is estimated that, with two years to run, Pienaar has turned his back on at least two million rand (250,000 pounds).
After being jettisoned by coach Andre Markgraaff, Pienaar took a month off and asked SARFU for permission to approach foreign clubs.

He will now find himself playing in front of around 6,000 spectators at the north London club's ground rather than the 60,000 audience which witnessed the World Cup triumph 18 months ago when Mandela wore a replica of his No 6 jersey.

As an employee of Saracens, Pienaar must now seek permission from them to play provincial rugby in South Africa during the English close season. But International Rugby Board (IRB) rules state that clubs must release players for internationals.

Under Pienaar, Transvaal won the Currie Cup twice and the inaugural Super 10 (now the Super 12). His 100th and possibly last game for the province was in this year's Currie Cup final at Ellis Park when Transvaal lost to Natal.
He has collected 29 caps since being chosen to captain South Africa on his test debut against France in Durban in 1993.
